transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the August 25 production policy review for the public API rate-limit project, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers, but per our normal review process, I need backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations to report your release-impacting findings before I record the final policy. The current draft has 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, the same limit applied to authentication endpoints, and no specified staffed launch window. I'd like to hear from each of you on whether you see any issues or concerns with this draft before I finalize it.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Backend's load replay shows the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I haven't updated the policy draft because the client test was owned by another team.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding for customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that its contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this is something Riley needs to account for before finalizing the policy.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The draft policy currently applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would be insufficient. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but Riley needs this before finalizing the policy.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from support operations. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated. Riley, this is the only staffed launch window we can support, and it aligns with the September 15 enforcement date Carlos mentioned, but the policy needs to specify this window so customers and internal teams know when staffed coverage is available.
transcript.speaker: A5
